key_insight: Cryogenic terahertz nanoscopy can directly map the bulk photovoltaic effect in dual-gated AB bilayer graphene, revealing how quantum geometry controls nonlinear photocurrent generation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a new diagnostic tool for optimizing optoelectronic devices by separating intrinsic photovoltaic response from contact and interface artifacts at deep-subwavelength scales.
method: Polarization-sensitive cryogenic terahertz microscopy with deep-subwavelength resolution
Dual-gated AB bilayer graphene measurements near band-gap/THz resonance
Carrier-density and temperature sweeps to probe symmetry-driven photocurrent behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports spatially resolved BPVE, twofold polarization symmetry, and agreement with theory, with evolution versus carrier density and temperature revealing trigonal warping and electron-hole asymmetry.
watch_item: The approach requires cryogenic, polarization-controlled THz microscopy, which may limit throughput and complicate translation to practical device screening.
paper_title: Terahertz nanoscopy of quantum-geometric photovoltaics in bilayer graphene
